info.album: The Very Best Of The Beach Boys: Sounds Of Summer

podcast.body: This song became a massive hit, peaking at number two on the charts and later being named Billboard's biggest hit of 1963. Brian Wilson drew inspiration from Chuck Berry's "Sweet Little Sixteen" for its melody and the concept of listing place names. With help from his girlfriend's brother and Mike Love, he transformed it into a song about surfing locations. Due to its close resemblance to Berry's track, Chuck Berry received the sole songwriting credit, resulting in a substantial financial benefit for him as "Surfin' USA" continues to be played on oldies radio, in commercials, and films. "Surfing USA will all be planning out a room. Surfing USA became a huge hit, reaching number two on the chart, and later being named by Billboard as the biggest hit of 1963."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 117: "Don't Worry Baby" by the Beach Boys

podcast.body: When initially released, songwriting credit was given solely to Brian Wilson. However, the melody was entirely lifted from Chuck Berry's 1958 song "Sweet Little Sixteen." Brian Wilson, with help from Mike Love, added new lyrics. Chuck Berry's music publisher pressured the band to add Chuck Berry's name to the songwriting credits, which has been the case since 1966. "When that song was released in 1963, the songwriting credit was listed as Brian Wilson of The Beach Boys. However, the melody was lifted entirely from a 1958 Chuck Berry song entitled Sweet Little X-D."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
